newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Key Brazil soybean areas hope for rain at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Key Brazil soybean areas hope for rain at weekend.

text.p: Rains were headed for Brazil's key soybean growing regions in the next three days and although most of the soybean crop was still safe, dryness in some areas threatened to cause losses, cooperatives said.
In Parana, growers were expecting scattered summer rains over the weekend. They said a cold front was due to arrive at the start of next week, bringing with it more widespread rains.
In Rio Grande do Sul, rains were still isolated causing sharp differences in soil moisture levels from region to region. Cooperatives said the next few days would bring more of the same.

"There are some dry regions here but it's still not a problem," said Volnei Zorzi at the Coorondinha cooperative in Rondinha. "But if it doesn't rain in the next 10 days we will have crop losses of 20 to 30 percent."
The most productive area in the region was also currently the driest, he said.
In Paim Filho, dryness during planting meant there was a disappointly low number of soybean plants per hectare.
"We're forecasting a 15 to 20 percent drop in the crop this year," said Leonidas Cesar Dutra of the Coppal cooperative. By contrast, conditions in Parana were optimal.
"Conditions are excellent," said Nelson Costa of the Parana cooperatives association Ocepar. "It's raining normally and soil moisture is good."

"We have some regions with high temperatures but this is not having a drastic effect on the development of the plants," he said, adding that temperatures reached 39 degrees Celsius during short periods of the day.
Sixty percent of the crop was still in the vegetative stage while 30 percent was in the flowering and pod formation phase. The remaining 10 percent was in the maturing phase.
